AbortReason.description:
The network error an aborted request reports to its page, under
Playwright's names.

Acted.description:
What a locator action answers once its input landed on its target:
nothing, since no operation returns a handle on an element (ADR 0085).

AppliedLimit.description:
A Limit that applies to a Run (ADRs 0041 and 0101): its scope's kind and
ID, what it caps, its period, what it allows, what is left of it and who
set it.

amount.description: What it allows per period: a count, or millionths of the currency.

currency.description: The currency it caps a price in, for a price Limit.

left.description: What is left of it in the current period.

period.description: Its period; none for a Limit that never starts again.

resets_at.description: When its period starts again; none for a Limit without one.

scope.description: What it is on; a scope kind this reader does not know is kept.

ArtifactId.description: Which Pinned artifact: its kind, its name and its build.

ArtifactKind.description:
What a Pinned artifact is (ADR 0098: the clean-up's rule covers every
kind). An entry of a kind the engine does not know is one it cannot read,
and keeps.

oneOf.description: A browser build, such as Chrome for Testing's.
The versioned copy of an executable a Daemon runs from (ADR 0024).
The engine executable a Product's Rust crate downloads (ADR 0051).

Asked.description: The format, with its default options.

entries.description: How many entries the log holds.

first_broken.description:
The first sequence that does not verify: an entry edited, missing
or out of its place, or, past the last entry, a tail the head file
says was there; none when intact.

intact.description:
Whether every entry chains to the one before it and the head file
agrees with the last one.

AxisReason.description: One reason a Run is not `verified` or not `complete` (ADR 0029).

call_id.description:
The AI task it is about, by its `callId`, when it is about one (ADR
0100).

code.description:
What it is, such as `stopped` or `failed`; a reason this reader does
not know is kept as it is.

Checkpoint.description:
A Checkpoint as the engine reports it (ADRs 0002, 0102 and 0116): a
consistent, self-contained copy of a Run's state, complete at its
location before it is reported, from which the Run resumes on this
machine or another one.

digest.description: The SHA-256 of its bytes, in lowercase hexadecimal.

journal_position.description:
The position of the run's journal it holds: how many commits of the
run file it contains. A resume from it redoes the work after.

location.description: Where it is: the file's path on the engine's machine.

run_epoch.description:
The run epoch of the writer that took it (ADR 0003), which a
destination compares and sets: one older than it holds is refused.

ClickParams.description: What `locator.click` takes: the locator whose element it clicks.

Completeness.description:
Whether a Run's results cover everything in its scope (ADRs 0005 and
0029).

oneOf.description: It finished, but the engine cannot vouch that nothing was missed.

keys.description:
The keys to explain, each a key or a prefix of keys, such as
`timeout`; every key when empty.

origin.description:
Where those run values come from: a scope's `settings` option by
default, or the CLI's flags when the CLI asks a Daemon.

project.description: The project configuration to explain with.

settings.description:
Run-layer values to explain with, as a Run's `settings` would give
them.

ConsoleFailure.description:
Why a Daemon's Console did not start: an Error code, its message and
what to do instead.

ConsoleState.description:
Where a Daemon's Console is, as its runtime file and `daemon status`
report it.

oneOf.description: The Console is served at this URL, such as `http://127.0.0.1:7801/`.
The Console did not start; the Daemon still serves its Clients.
The engine carries no Console, as an SDK crate's linked engine.

DaemonEndpoint.description:
Where a Daemon or an Attached engine's private endpoint listens (ADR
0024): a `0600` Unix socket on macOS and Linux, loopback TCP on
Windows.

DaemonHealth.description:
What `daemon.health` answers: what the ops listener's `/livez` and
`/readyz` check (ADR 0050). In a Daemon group, readiness ignores the
Lead Daemon's reachability.

live.description:
Whether it is live: its runtime and its Runs' registry, which writes
their run state, respond.

ready.description: Whether it is ready: live, and able to take a new Run.

unready.description: Why it is not ready, when it is not; empty when it is.

clients.description: How many Clients are connected, the caller and Consoles included.

console.description: Where its Console is served, or why it is not.

kept_alive.description:
Whether it never stops idle: `--keep-alive`, a held Schedule or an
installed service.

live_runs.description: How many of its Runs are live.

product.description: The Product the Daemon runs as.

DaemonStopping.description: What `daemon.stop` answers, before the Daemon stops.

live_runs.description: How many live Runs it stops, each resumable from its own state.

total_bytes.description: The bytes the answer announced, when it did.

EndingError.description: An Error code a Run's ending raises, with its message and details.

product.description: The Product the engine runs as.

product_major.description: The major of its Product version, which names its per-major state.

protocol_version.description: The protocol version the engine speaks.

EngineInstance.description: One engine process, new each time an engine starts: the positions of its events count within it. A Client compares it for equality only.

ErrorData.description:
What a failure's `data` holds: its Error code, whether the same call may
succeed when made again, and the code's own details.

code.description: The Error code, or the name of the protocol failure.

retryable.description: Whether the same call may succeed when made again.

after.description:
The last event the Client read, `{engine_instance, position}`: the
subscription resumes after it, or starts with `events.resync` when
the engine no longer holds it or another engine instance gave it, as
after a Daemon restart. Absent, it starts with the next event.

ExplainedSetting.description: One setting as `config explain` shows it.

applied.description:
Whether this engine applies it: `false` for a key only the other
Product honours, which a shared file may hold (ADR 0087).

cap.description: An Operator policy's cap on it, if any.

locked_by.description:
The layer that locked it, if any: an Operator policy's lock, a
Recipe that declares it without exposing it, or the default for an
honesty guarantee.

origin.description: For the run layer, where the value came from.

products.description: The Products that honour it, from its Product mark (ADR 0095).

value.description:
The effective value, or for a key this engine does not apply, the
value its highest layer wrote.

weakens.description:
Whether its value weakens a guarantee class or switches off a costly
control, which the results it touches are marked with (ADR 0028).

FillParams.description:
What `locator.fill` takes: the locator whose field it fills, and the
text.

value.description: The text the field holds afterwards; an empty text clears it.

FormatsParams.description: What `page.formats` takes: the page, and the formats it asks for.

FormatsRequest.description:
The formats a `page.formats` call asks for, each `true` or its options:
one value, which a Record can carry and a Dataset's schema can be
generated from (ADR 0103). A format left out is left out of the result.

markdown.description: The page's content as Markdown, with GFM's tables.

GotoParams.description:
What `page.goto` takes: the page, the URL it goes to, and when it
answers.

wait_until.description: When the navigation answers; `load` when absent.

KeyValueStoreDeleted.description: What `key_value_store.delete` answers once the key is gone.

KeyValueStoreKeyParams.description:
What `key_value_store.get` and `key_value_store.delete` take: the Run
and the key.

run_id.description: The Run whose store it is.

KeyValueStoreKeysEnded.description: What `key_value_store.keys` answers once it sent its last key.

KeyValueStoreKeysParams.description:
What `key_value_store.keys` takes: the Run, and the prefix every key it
sends starts with.

prefix.description: The prefix of the keys it sends; every key when left out.

run_id.description: The Run whose store it is.

KeyValueStoreSet.description: What `key_value_store.set` answers once the value is committed.

KeyValueStoreSetParams.description: What `key_value_store.set` takes: the Run, the key and its value.

run_id.description: The Run whose store it is.

value.description:
The value: any JSON but a top-level null, which `value_invalid`
refuses; a nested null is kept.

KeyValueStoreValue.description:
What `key_value_store.get` answers: the key's committed value, or null
when the key is absent.

value.description: The value, or null for an absent key.

KindUsage.description: What a Run used of one Usage kind.

amount.description: A count, or millionths of the currency.

currency.description: The currency, an ISO 4217 code; none for a count.

usage_kind.description: The Usage kind, a value of a type both Products share.

LastRead.description:
The last event a Client read: its position, and the engine instance
that gave it.

engine_instance.description: The engine instance, as its `hello` named it.

oneOf.description:
It ended early: by a Limit, an abort, its timeout, the loss of its
engine or exhausted resources.
An error in the engine or the program's code ended it.

Limit.description:
One Limit of the Usage ledger: a generic row, which a newer engine may
write with a scope kind, a Usage kind, a currency or a period this one
does not know (ADR 0041).

amount.description:
How much it allows per period: a count of the Usage kind, or
millionths of the currency.

currency.description:
The currency it caps the Usage kind's price in, an ISO 4217 code;
none for a Limit on the Usage itself.

must_understand.description:
Whether an engine that cannot evaluate it must refuse the runs it
cannot place outside it, with `limit_not_understood`.

period.description:
The period it counts over; none for a Limit that never starts again,
such as a Client connection's.

usage_kind.description: The Usage kind it caps, a value of a type both Products share.

LimitScope.description:
What a Limit is on: a scope kind, a value of a type both Products share
(`install`, `daemon`, `person`, `token`, `connection`, and Foxhound's
`partitioned_crawl`), and which one of its kind (ADR 0041). A kind this
reader does not know is kept as it is.

id.description:
Which one of its kind: the major's name for a Daemon, the person's
name, the token's name or the Client connection's ID; empty for the
install.

LimitSetter.description: Who set a Limit, which decides whether it allows paying (ADR 0045).

oneOf.description: A person, in the Console or an interactive CLI prompt.
A Client, which only adds a Limit of its own.

LimitStanding.description: What the engine that read a Limit makes of it.

oneOf.description: It holds its runs to it.

It is on a value only Foxhound carries, such as `paid_fetch`, which
a Collie engine keeps untouched (ADR 0098).
It cannot evaluate it: a newer engine wrote it.

LimitUsage.description: One Limit with the Usage counted against it in its current period.

charged.description:
The Usage charged in the current period: what ended runs used, and
what was reclaimed from dead engines' Slices.

held.description: The Usage live runs hold in Slices they have not returned yet.

left.description: What is left of the amount in the current period.

managed_major.description:
The major of the managed Operator policy whose row it is; none for
a row no managed policy wrote.

period_started_at.description: When the current period started; none for a Limit without one.

resets_at.description: When the next period starts; none for a Limit without one.

standing.description: What the engine that read it makes of it.

Locator.description:
A locator (ADR 0085): what an action looks for on a page, resolved
again at each use, never a handle on an element. This tracer's locators
are CSS selectors.

selector.description: A CSS selector, which also matches inside open shadow roots.

LogLevel.description:
The level of the engine's log events a Connection receives: those at
it and above; `off`, the default, receives none.

oneOf.description: State changes, warnings and errors: what `info` logs.
Also a line per request, fetch or command.

MainContent.description: Whether the extractor found the document's main content.

oneOf.description:
The document has none: the formats read from it are empty, a value
and never the whole page in its place.

MarkdownContent.description: How much of the page a Markdown format holds.

oneOf.description: The main content the extractor finds, the default.

MarkdownFormat.description: The `markdown` format of a request: `true`, or its options.

content.description: How much of the page it holds.

calls.description: The calls, retries and Repairs included.

Navigated.description:
What a navigation answers: the document's response, or none for a
navigation within the same document, to a URL no server answers, such as
`about:blank`, to a file the browser downloads instead of showing, which
`page.download` reports, or back or forward from the last entry of the
page's history. A 404 or a 500 is a response, a value.

NewPageParams.description: What `run.new_page` takes: the Run whose default Session opens the page.

NotUnderstoodLimit.description:
A Limit flagged *must understand* that a Run's engine cannot evaluate,
as the Run stopped for it names it (ADR 0041): its scope, Usage kind,
currency and period as the ledger holds them.

currency.description: The currency it caps a price in, for a price Limit.

period.description: Its period; none for a Limit that never starts again.

NothingDone.description: Why a call that ends a Run did nothing (ADR 0102's G1).

oneOf.description: The start found the Run ended.

No seed reached a handler: each was refused when added or skipped
when fetched.
A resume or a retry found nothing left.

PageBodyParams.description: What `page.body` takes: the body to read.

run_id.description: The Run whose folder holds it.

PageBodyRead.description: What `page.body` answers once it sent the last chunk.

PageDownload.description:
What `page.download` reports: a navigation of a page that the browser
turned into a download.

page_id.description: The page whose navigation it was.

suggested_filename.description: The file name the browser suggests for it.

PageFormats.description:
What `page.formats` answers: the formats the request asked for, and
none it did not, with the document's URL, its base URL and whether it
has main content. Text is as the document holds it, never repaired.

base_url.description:
The URL its relative URLs resolve against: its first `<base href>`,
else its URL.

markdown.description: Its content as Markdown, when the request asked for it.

PageId.description: A page of a Run, named by the engine when it opens it.

PageOpened.description:
What `run.new_page` answers: the page, and the Session it belongs to,
which `page.session()` returns.

session_id.description: Its Session: the Run's default Session.

PageResponse.description: The response to a request of a page, such as a navigation's document.

encoding.description:
For a navigation's document, the encoding the browser decoded it
with, as `document.characterSet` names it, such as `Shift_JIS` (ADR
0119); none for another response, and for a navigation that answered
at `commit`, before its document was decoded.

headers.description: Its headers, their names lower-cased, as the browser received them.

PageRouteParams.description:
What `page.route` takes: the page, and the URLs whose requests its
handler answers.

Period.description:
The period a Limit counts over, in an explicit IANA time zone, so that
it never depends on the host's (ADR 0041).

time_zone.description: The IANA time zone its midnights are in, such as `Europe/Paris`.

PeriodLength.description: How long a period Limit counts before it starts again (ADR 0041).

oneOf.description: From one midnight to the next.
From Monday's midnight to the next Monday's.
From the first day's midnight to the next month's.

PlanReport.description: What a Run did with its Plan file (ADR 0091).

file.description: The Plan file's path, or none.

status.description: What became of its new versions.

steps_changed.description: The steps that changed, each Agent task one entry (ADR 0100).

PlanStatus.description: What became of a Run's new Plan versions (ADR 0091).

oneOf.description: They were written to the Plan file.

PluginRun.description: A Plugin that ran in a Run (ADRs 0016 and 0033).

confinement_missing.description:
The parts of its confinement the host could not give, under a
reduced confinement the Operator policy allowed.

network_level.description: The network level it ran at.

PointInTime.description: A point in time in UTC, as RFC 3339.

Position.description: An event's position among every event of one engine, which only goes up.

PressParams.description:
What `locator.press` takes: the locator whose element gets the key, and
the key.

key.description:
A key or a combination, such as `Enter`, `a` or `Shift+Tab`, by
Playwright's key names.

Product.description:
One of Goodfetch's two Products (ADR 0084), by its mark as the catalog
writes it.

ProductVersion.description: A Product version, `major.minor.patch` with an optional pre-release (ADR 0090).

ProgressMessage.description: A program's own status line about its Run (RT-15).

ProjectSettings.description:
A project configuration's values, which a Client reads where it runs and
sends with a scope it opens (ADR 0083).

path.description: The file's path, as the Client found it.

settings.description: Its settings, nested as the file nests them.

ReachedLimit.description:
The Limit a Run cannot take more of: what `limit_reached` details, and
what a Run stopped for it names (ADR 0041).

currency.description: The currency it caps a price in, for a price Limit.

period.description: Its period; none for a Limit that never starts again.

resets_at.description: When its period starts again; none for a Limit without one.

RecordingReport.description: What a Run did with the Response recording its start named (ADR 0105).

recorded_from.description: When the oldest of them was fetched.

recorded_to.description: When the newest of them was fetched.

responses_used.description: How many recorded responses it used.

RequestFailed.description:
What `page.request_failed` reports: a request of the run that failed
while no call waited for it, such as one the egress policy refused.

failure.description:
Why it failed: the Error code a call waiting for it would have
raised, with its details, such as `egress_refused`.

url.description: The request's URL, as the run gave it.

RequestId.description: A request's id, which its reply carries back.

Resource.description: A resource the governor can run out of (ADR 0122).

oneOf.description: The machine's or the container's memory.
A filesystem the Run writes to.

Resync.description:
What `events.resync` gives: the current state, from which the stream
continues.

runs.description: The axes of each Run the engine knows, live or ended.

RouteAbortParams.description: What `route.abort` takes: the request, and the error its page sees.

RouteAnswered.description: What an answer to a route answers once the engine acted on it.

RouteEnded.description: What a route's subscription answers when its page or Session closes.

RouteFetched.description:
What `route.fetch` answers: the response the request got, its body
kept, for the handler to pass to `route.fulfill`.

RouteFulfillParams.description:
What `route.fulfill` takes: the request, and the response the program
answers it with; nothing reaches the network.

body.description: Its body, in Base64; empty when absent.

RouteHandleParams.description:
What `route.handle` gives the handler: the request, named by the ID its
answer passes.

id.description:
The id of the `page.route` or `session.route` call whose handler is
asked.

page_id.description: The page that sent the request.

route_id.description: The intercepted request, which an answer names.

RouteHandled.description:
What the handler replies to `route.handle` once it ended; a failure
reply says it failed.

RouteId.description:
One intercepted request a route's handler answers, which `route.*`
names.

RouteOverridesParams.description:
What `route.continue`, `route.fallback` and `route.fetch` take: the
request, and what to send instead of what it carries. Each override
replaces its part whole; a header value may hold a Secret placeholder
(ADR 0092).

headers.description: Other headers, in place of every header the request carries.

url.description: Another URL, judged again by the domain policy.

RouteRequest.description:
A request as a route sees it: as the page sent it, with the overrides of
the routes that fell back before. The engine's own additions, such as
the Session's cookies, come after every route, so none is here.

headers.description: Its headers, as the page sent them.

is_navigation_request.description: Whether it loads the document of the page's main frame.

resource_type.description:
What the page loads with it, as the browser names it, such as
`Document`, `Script` or `XHR`.

RunAbortParams.description: What `run.abort` takes: the Run, and whether the abort was forwarded.

forwarded.description:
Set by an engine that forwards the abort to the owner the Run index
names (ADR 0031): an engine that does not own the Run then answers
`run_not_owned` instead of taking its writer role.

RunAxes.description:
A Run's three axes as they are now (ADR 0029): what
`run.axes_changed` reports, and what a resync gives of each Run.

completeness.description: Whether its results cover its scope, once it ended.

verdict.description: Whether its own checks prove what it committed, once it ended.

location.description:
Where to write the Checkpoint, a path on the engine's machine; by
default where the engine keeps the Run's Checkpoints, its own folder.

run_epoch.description: The run epoch the Checkpoint is taken under.

RunId.description: A Run ID (ADR 0036): lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, starting and ending with a letter or a digit, never a name Windows reserves for a device.

RunOrigin.description: Where a run-layer value came from (ADR 0083).

RunProgress.description: A Run's progress as it is now (ADR 0102): what `run.progress` reports.

message.description: The program's own status line, once it set one.

RunReport.description:
What a Run states about itself when it ends (ADR 0102). A part no area
supplied is absent, never zero.

checkpoint.description: The last Checkpoint written of it in this engine, when one was.

completeness.description: Whether its results cover its scope.

completeness_reasons.description: Why it is not `complete`, when it is not.

console_url.description:
Its page in the Console, where its Run trace replays, when the
engine knows a Console address (ADR 0031).

error.description:
The error the call that ends it raises: the one that failed a
`failed` Run, or a write at its end that failed, such as its Plan
file's (ADR 0116).

nothing_done.description: Why the call that answered it did nothing, when it did nothing.

plan.description: What it did with its Plan file (ADR 0091).

policy_version.description:
The version of the Operator policy it ran under, when one applied
(ADR 0031).

recording.description: What it did with the Response recording its start named (ADR 0105).

settings.description:
Each effective value it ran with, the layer that set it and the one
that locked it, as `config.explain` gives them (ADR 0028).

stop_reason.description: Why it stopped, when it did.

uncertain_effects.description:
Each Effect it left uncertain, until a person reconciles it (ADR
0106).

usage.description:
What it used, as the Usage ledger charged it, with the Limits that
apply to it (ADR 0101).

verdict.description: Whether its own checks prove what it committed.

verdict_reasons.description: Why it is not `verified`, when it is not.

warnings.description: What the areas warn of, each with a code and a message.

weakened.description: Every setting that weakened a safeguard for it (ADR 0028).

checkpoint.description:
A Checkpoint to resume from, a path on the engine's machine, which
becomes the Run's state in this engine's run folder; by default the
Run resumes from its run file on this machine.

project.description: The project configuration the Client found, layer 3 (ADR 0083).

settings.description:
The Run's settings from the resume on, nested by key: the run layer
(ADRs 0083 and 0102).

message.description: The program's status line, which replaces the one before.

project.description: The project configuration the Client found, layer 3 (ADR 0083).

run_id.description:
The Run's ID; the engine generates a lowercase ULID when it is
absent. An existing ID returns that Run when the caller and the
inputs match, and fails with `run_conflict` otherwise.

settings.description: The Run's settings, nested by key: the run layer (ADR 0083).

RunStarted.description: What a start answers once its Run is started, never at its end.

needs.description:
The Product it needs (ADR 0098): Collie until it uses an entry the
catalog marks Foxhound's, Foxhound from then on.

RunUsage.description:
What a Run used, as the Usage ledger charged it, and the Limits that
apply to it (ADRs 0041 and 0101): what `run.usage` answers and the
report carries.

browser_time.description: How long it held a browser, in milliseconds.

limits.description: Each Limit that applies to it, with what is left of it.

other.description:
What it used of a Usage kind this engine does not name, kept as the
ledger holds it.

proxy_bytes.description: The bytes it sent and received through a proxy.

uncapped.description:
Whether it spent, or reserved, money in a currency no Limit holding
it caps (ADR 0041): *uncapped*.

RunWaitParams.description:
What `run.finish` and `run.stop` take: the Run, and how long the call
waits for its end.

timeout.description:
How long the call waits for the Run's end, in milliseconds; past it,
it fails with `deadline_exceeded` and only the wait ends. None by
default for `run.finish`, which the Run's own `timeout.run` bounds;

RunWarning.description:
What a Run warns of (ADR 0102): a code of the warning table, or of a
newer engine's, kept as it is, with its message and what it concerns.

key.description: The key to keep the value under.

SampleStorePutResult.description: What a sample store answers once it kept a value.

replaced.description: Whether a value was already kept under the key.

SessionId.description: A Session of a Run, named by the engine when it opens it.

SessionRouteParams.description:
What `session.route` takes: the Session, and the URLs whose requests its
handler answers, on every page of the Session.

SettingsExplanation.description:
What `config.explain` answers and `config explain --json` prints:
every setting's effective value, the layer that set it and the layer
that locked it (ADR 0028), and the files read.

files.description: The files of the configuration layers, lowest first.

policy_version.description:
The Operator policy's version, `sha256:` and the first 16 hex digits
of its file's digest, which the run report names; `None` without a
policy.

settings.description: Each setting, by key.

SettingsFile.description: A layer's file, as `config explain` names it.

found.description: Whether it exists; a missing file sets nothing.

SettingsLayer.description: The layers settings resolve through, lowest first (ADRs 0028 and 0083).

oneOf.description:
The run: a program's settings, a call's argument, a CLI flag or an
Integration's form.

StartedAs.description: Whether a start began its Run or found it.

oneOf.description:
Its Run ID named a Run started before with the same inputs, which is
returned as it is.

It was interrupted and goes on from its committed state, its run
file or a Checkpoint, at the next run epoch (ADRs 0002, 0003 and
0102).

Its program, a person or a Client aborted it, a Connection's close
included (ADR 0078).

It was paused: checkpointed and stopped, to be resumed by its Run ID
(RT-11).

It was migrated: checkpointed and stopped, to be resumed from its
Checkpoint on another machine (ADR 0002).

Its `timeout.run` passed, and it stopped at its next safe point,
resumable with a fresh clock (ADR 0080); no Error code of its own.

Its foreground Daemon drained on `SIGTERM`: checkpointed and
stopped, to be resumed by its Run ID on the Daemon's next start
(ADR 0049).

It could not take another Slice of a Limit, and stopped at its next
safe point, resumable once the period starts again or a person
raises the Limit (ADR 0041).

A Limit flagged *must understand* that its engine cannot evaluate
came to cover it when it charged, and it stopped at its next safe
point, resumable by an engine that can (ADR 0041): the stop of the
Error code `limit_not_understood`.

folder.description: For storage, the folder whose filesystem filled.

Tags.description: A Run's tags, in the order given.

Baggage. The schema checks only that each is a string: a receiver drops

holds it.

tracestate.description:

crawl_request.description: The crawl request it ran for, in a crawl.

first_command.description: The first command sent for it.

instruction.description: Its instruction, for an AI action.

key.description: Its key, for a declared Effect.

oneOf.description: Its run state cannot be written.

one, or a regular expression in the `regex` crate's syntax. A predicate

oneOf.description: A regular expression, matched anywhere in the URL.

amount.description:

currency.description: The currency it caps the price in, an ISO 4217 code.

scope_id.description:

Every check the Run relies on passed, none was switched off, and no

When a navigation answers, by the state its document reached

Once the browser committed the document, its response received: a

error_codes.description: The host has addresses only in an IP family the Session holds no local address of, such as IPv6 addresses for a Session bound to an IPv4 address. Add a local address of that family to the run's local addresses, or reach the host another way.
error_codes.name: address_family_unavailable

error_codes.description: A pinned download the call needed failed: the network, an HTTP status, or bytes whose digest is not the pinned one. Retry, or install beforehand with the Product's `browsers install`, or point `GOODFETCH_BROWSERS_PATH` at a prepared cache.
error_codes.name: artifact_download_failed

error_codes.description: The `offline` setting refused a pinned download the call needed. Run the Product's `browsers install` beforehand where the cache is writable, point `GOODFETCH_BROWSERS_PATH` at a prepared cache, or lift `offline` where it was set.
error_codes.name: artifact_unavailable_offline

error_codes.description: The Run's folder holds no body of this ID: the Run or the body is unknown, or the ID is not a body's.
error_codes.name: body_not_found

error_codes.description: The Browser host the engine reached is of a version this engine cannot drive. Upgrade the Browser host, which either Product's executable runs as its `browser-host` command.
error_codes.name: browser_host_outdated

error_codes.description: The browser's build is installed, but it did not start or did not open the page: it exited, or its connection refused or fell silent. The details name its executable and how it ended.
error_codes.name: browser_launch_failed

error_codes.description: The browser build a launch needs is not in the Browser cache and the engine cannot write that cache, such as an image's read-only `GOODFETCH_BROWSERS_PATH`; or a browser named by channel or path is not there. Run the Product's `browsers install` where the cache is writable, install the browser of that channel, or correct the path.
error_codes.name: browser_not_installed

error_codes.description: The call was stopped in flight, at its next cancellation point: its Client sent `$/cancel`, or what it needed was closed under it.
error_codes.name: call_cancelled

error_codes.description: The call was made on a value its program had closed: a Connection, or a Run, Session or Page under it. A value never reopens: connect again, or start the Run again by its Run ID.
error_codes.name: closed

error_codes.description: The Connection to the engine dropped before the call was answered, so whether it took effect is unknown. The Client connects again by itself; make the call again once it has, after checking that an Effect did not happen.
error_codes.name: connection_lost

error_codes.description: The Console did not start: another program holds the port of `console.address`. The Daemon still serves its Clients. Stop the other program, or set `console.address` to a free port (port 0 takes any free one) and restart the Daemon.
error_codes.name: console_port_in_use

error_codes.description: The foreground Daemon is draining on `SIGTERM`: it takes no run and checkpoints every live run as resumable, then exits. Start or resume the run on the Daemon that replaces it.
error_codes.name: daemon_draining

error_codes.description: The call's deadline passed before what it waited for came, such as a response's first byte or a navigation. Its `limit` names the timeout's setting, its value and the layer that set it: raise that setting, or wait for the right thing.
error_codes.name: deadline_exceeded

error_codes.description: The run's egress policy refused a request before it connected: a host the domain policy does not allow, an address that is not globally reachable, or a scheme no request may use. The details name the URL, the rule, the address when there is one and the setting that would allow it.
error_codes.name: egress_refused

error_codes.description: The Attached engine ended before its Connection was closed, so the call has no answer. Its details carry the exit code or signal and the last 64 KiB of its stderr.
error_codes.name: engine_exited

error_codes.description: `connect()` found no engine executable to start: the Product's engine-path variable names no executable, or the Product's platform package is not installed. The `fix` names the variable or the package.
error_codes.name: engine_not_found

error_codes.description: The engine wrote a line that is not one JSON-RPC message on the Connection, such as a log line on an Attached engine's stdout, so the Client ended the Connection. A bug in Goodfetch: report it with the line its details carry.
error_codes.name: engine_output_invalid

error_codes.description: Windows refused to start the file: Smart App Control, or another App Control policy, blocks executables without a signature or reputation it trusts. Goodfetch never re-signs a file it did not build. For a browser, use the Goodfetch Chromium or an installed Chrome by channel; otherwise turn Smart App Control off, or ask the device's administrator to allow the file.
error_codes.name: executable_blocked_by_smart_app_control

error_codes.description: The bytes of a file could not be written: no space or quota left, or an I/O error, or any failure where the engine keeps its files. No partial file is left. Free space where the files go, or ask the Daemon's operator, then make the same call again.
error_codes.name: file_write_failed

error_codes.description: A file, such as a run state or a Checkpoint, is of a format version this engine cannot read: a newer minor or major, written by a newer engine, which `fix` says to upgrade to, or an older major, which `upgrade-files` upgrades. The file is left as it is.
error_codes.name: format_version_unsupported

error_codes.description: A newer engine wrote a Limit this engine cannot evaluate, and it may cover the run; the details name it. Upgrade the engine.
error_codes.name: limit_not_understood

error_codes.description: A Limit that covers the run has nothing left in its period; the details name its scope, its Usage kind, its period and when it starts again. Wait for the next period, or ask a person to raise it.
error_codes.name: limit_reached

error_codes.description: The engine's own resolver got no usable answer for the host name: its name servers timed out, refused the query, failed or could not be reached. Check the name servers of the system's resolver configuration, or map the name with the `resolve` setting.
error_codes.name: name_lookup_failed

error_codes.description: The resolver found no address for the host name. The engine's own resolver, used on Linux and for Sessions with a local address, reads the system's resolver configuration and hosts file but asks neither NSS modules (such as a directory service or a VPN client's) nor multicast DNS, so a name only they resolve, such as a `.local` name, fails here. Map such a name to its address with the `resolve` setting, or correct the name.
error_codes.name: name_not_resolved

error_codes.description: The navigation reached no document: the browser's network error, such as `net::ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED`, is in the details, or the browser failed it for a reason it did not name.
error_codes.name: navigation_failed

error_codes.description: Another navigation of the page started before this one committed, so this one reached no document: the page went where the other took it.
error_codes.name: navigation_interrupted

error_codes.description: The call asks a Daemon about itself, and this engine is an Attached engine. Ask the Daemon of the major, found through its runtime file, or run `daemon status`.
error_codes.name: not_a_daemon

error_codes.description: The running engine's Product does not carry what was asked: a Client that needs Foxhound reached a Collie engine, or a call, a setting or a value only Foxhound carries reached one. Run it with Foxhound, which contains everything Collie does, or connect to a Foxhound engine.
error_codes.name: not_in_product

error_codes.description: The page's renderer crashed, or its browser process was lost while the call ran; `browser_exit` says how the browser ended when it is what was lost. The page is gone: open another.
error_codes.name: page_crashed

error_codes.description: A handler the program gave a page failed, such as a route's handler that threw: its request was aborted unless it was answered already, never sent half-changed, and its route was removed. Raised by the call that waited on that request, such as the `goto` whose document it was, or else by the next call on its page. The details name the handler, the request's URL and what the failure said.
error_codes.name: page_handler_failed

error_codes.description: The path the program chose cannot be written for a reason the path causes: permission denied, a read-only filesystem, a folder at the path, a file where a parent folder should be, a name the filesystem refuses, a file too large for that filesystem, or a path not found once its parents are made. No partial file is left. Change the path.
error_codes.name: path_not_writable

error_codes.description: A URL pattern the engine cannot match: a regular expression with look-around, a back-reference or another construct outside the `regex` crate's syntax, or a glob with nested or unmatched braces. The details name the construct; match the URL with a predicate instead, which runs in the program.
error_codes.name: pattern_unsupported

error_codes.description: Only a person gives this answer, in the Console or an interactive CLI prompt: no agent surface, SDK, script or command run under `--json` or without a terminal may. Answer it in the Console, or run the command in a terminal.
error_codes.name: person_required

error_codes.description: The engine does not speak the protocol version the Client's `hello` names: it accepts its own major with the same or an older minor. Upgrade the older side.
error_codes.name: protocol_version_unsupported

error_codes.description: The engine ran out of memory or storage for the Run: it checkpointed and stopped it, or refused to start it where its run file would go. The details name the `resource`. Resume it once memory or space frees up, on an engine with a larger allowance, or with lower ceilings.
error_codes.name: resources_exhausted

error_codes.description: The response's body broke off before its end: shorter than its `Content-Length`, a chunked body without its last chunk, or a stream the server or the connection ended. A navigation waiting for `domcontentloaded` or `load` raises it for its main document; one that answered at `commit` leaves it to the body's read. The details name the URL and the bytes received and expected.
error_codes.name: response_truncated

error_codes.description: The route's request was answered already, by an earlier `continue`, `fulfill`, `abort` or `fallback`, or its handler ended: the first answer stands and this one changed nothing.
error_codes.name: route_already_handled

error_codes.description: Another engine holds the Run's writer lock, and the owner the Run index names did not take the action: it did not answer, or does not own the Run. The engine retried the lock 5 times over about a second; the writer may end, so try again later.

error_codes.description: The Run ID names a Run started with other inputs, or by another caller; the details list each difference. Start under another Run ID.

error_codes.description: The Run ID is not one the engine takes: lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, at most 128, starting and ending with a letter or a digit, never a name Windows reserves for a device.

error_codes.description: Another engine holds the Run's writer lock, so this one cannot write the Run; the other may end.

error_codes.description: No Run has this Run ID: the Run index does not list it.
error_codes.name: run_not_found

error_codes.description: The action was forwarded to this engine as the Run's owner, and this engine does not own the Run: the Run index named an engine that has since ended or restarted. The engine that forwarded it retries the Run's writer lock.

error_codes.description: The Run's state is missing, damaged or cannot be written at its location; the details give the path. The engine never starts afresh under that Run ID.

error_codes.description: A Secret provider gave no value for a reference: a missing variable, a locked keychain, an unreachable vault, the caller's `resolveSecret` missing or throwing, no answer within `timeout.secret`. `failure` says which, and the details name the placeholder or setting, the reference and the provider, never a value.

error_codes.description: No scope binds the Secret placeholder a call names. `bound` lists the placeholders bound, never a value.

error_codes.description: A value of the wrong type or out of the setting's own range, an empty or unparsable deployment variable, or a settings file that does not parse.

error_codes.description: A value a lower layer locked or capped, outside a Recipe's exposed bounds, or one only a lower layer may set or widen, such as `tls.trusted_cas` from a run. `limit` names the setting and the layer that holds it.

error_codes.description: A key no Product knows, or an unknown `GOODFETCH_` variable. The message names the closest valid one.

error_codes.description: The locator still matched several elements when the action's timeout passed, so the action did nothing. The details list every match, each with a locator that reaches it alone, and `limit` names the timeout's setting; a longer timeout would not fix the locator.

error_codes.description: The navigation followed as many redirects as it may and was redirected again, as a redirect loop is: the browser's count is 20 requests in a navigation's chain, its first included, so Chromium follows 19 redirects. error_codes.description: The Key-value store refused the key or its value: a key must be 1 to 512 Unicode scalar values with no control character, and a value any JSON but null, which `get` answers for an absent key; remove a key with `delete`. The details name the key and say which was refused.

operations.description: Verifies the user's Audit log: every entry's hash chains it to the one before it, and the head file names the last one. Answers that it is intact, or the first sequence that does not verify, so an edited, deleted, reordered or truncated entry, a truncated tail included, shows.

operations.description: Shows each setting's effective value, the layer that set it and the layer that locked it, from the built-in defaults, the Operator policy, user configuration and the project configuration and run values given, and lists the keys only the other Product honours as that Product's.
operations.name: config.explain

operations.description: Sets the level of the engine's log events this Connection receives as `$/log` notifications, from the next one on: `off`, `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug` or `trace`, as `hello`'s `log_level` set it first. Each Connection has its own. Log events are telemetry: one the Connection is too slow to receive is dropped, and the next counts it in `dropped`.
operations.name: connection.set_log_level

operations.description: Says whether the Daemon is live and ready to take a new Run, and why not: what its ops listener's `/livez` and `/readyz` answer with a status alone.
operations.name: daemon.health

operations.description: Says what the Daemon runs as, where it listens, how many Clients and live Runs it has, and when it stops idle.
operations.name: daemon.status

operations.description: Stops the Daemon once it answered: its live Runs stop, each resumable from its own state, and its runtime file and socket are removed.

operations.description: Says which Product the engine runs as, its Product version and major, and the protocol version it speaks.
operations.name: engine.info

operations.description: Subscribes to the engine's events. The call stays in flight, sending its events in `$/events` batches, never more than the credits granted with `$/credit`, until it is cancelled. No producer waits for a subscription: a lossless event is never dropped unseen, and a subscription whose queue is full falls behind, dropping its queued lossless events, and next sends `events.resync`, then the stream. A telemetry event is coalesced with the unsent one of the same kind and scope, and counts it as `dropped`. Given `after`, the last event read, it resumes after it, or starts with `events.resync` when the engine no longer holds it or another engine instance gave it, as after a Daemon restart.
operations.name: events.subscribe

operations.description: Removes a key from a live Run's Key-value store and answers whether it existed.
operations.name: key_value_store.delete

operations.description: Answers the value a Run's Key-value store holds for a key, as committed, or null when the key is absent. Takes no writer lock, so it reads a Run no program holds without resuming it.
operations.name: key_value_store.get

operations.description: Sends the committed keys of a Run's Key-value store that start with `prefix`, in the order of their Unicode scalar values, in `$/key` notifications, one per credit granted with `$/credit`, then answers how many it sent. Takes no writer lock.
operations.name: key_value_store.keys

operations.description: Commits a JSON value for a key in a live Run's Key-value store, replacing the one it held: the last commit wins. A null value fails with `value_invalid`; remove a key with `delete`.
operations.name: key_value_store.set

operations.description: Clicks the element the locator matches once it is unique, visible, enabled, stable and receiving the click (the guard, ADR 0019); a click that lands on another element is cancelled and sent again, until `timeout.action` passes.
operations.name: locator.click

operations.description: Replaces the text of the field the locator matches, once it is unique, visible, enabled and editable, with text the page receives as typed input, until `timeout.action` passes.
operations.name: locator.fill

operations.description: Focuses the element the locator matches, once it is unique, visible and enabled, and presses a key or a combination on it as a keyboard does, until `timeout.action` passes.
operations.name: locator.press

operations.description: Reads a page body by its handle, for a Client that cannot read the handle's file: sends the body in `$/chunk` notifications of at most 64 KiB, one per credit granted with `$/credit`, then answers its size.
operations.name: page.body

operations.description: Reads the formats a request names from the page's current document, each read from one serialization of it, and answers only those, with the document's URL, its base URL and whether it has main content. A document with no main content answers empty formats and `main_content: "none"`, a value. It needs neither layout nor pixels, so every tier serves it.
operations.name: page.formats

operations.description: Goes back one entry in the page's history and waits for its `load` event, answering the document's response, or none when there is no entry to go back to. The back/forward cache is off, so the document always loads again (ADR 0121).
operations.name: page.go_back

operations.description: Goes forward one entry in the page's history and waits for its `load` event, answering the document's response, or none when there is no entry to go forward to. The back/forward cache is off, so the document always loads again (ADR 0121).
operations.name: page.go_forward

operations.description: Navigates the page to a URL and waits for its document's `load` event, or the state `wait_until` names, answering the document's response: a 404 or a 500 is a response, a value. A file the browser downloads, such as a PDF, answers no response and emits `page.download`. A navigation that reaches no document raises `navigation_failed`, one another navigation supersedes before it committed `navigation_interrupted`, a redirect loop `too_many_redirects`, and a document whose body broke off `response_truncated`, unless the navigation answered at `commit`.
operations.name: page.goto

operations.description: Loads the page's document again and waits for its `load` event, answering the document's response: a 404 or a 500 is a response, a value. A navigation that reaches no document raises `navigation_failed`, and one another navigation supersedes before it committed `navigation_interrupted`.
operations.name: page.reload

operations.description: Routes the page's requests whose URL matches to the program, armed when the call arrives: the call stays in flight, and for each such request the engine sends `route.handle`, which the handler answers with `route.continue`, `route.fulfill`, `route.abort`, `route.fallback`, or `route.fetch` then `route.fulfill`. Page routes come before Session routes, later routes first, and the first answer wins; a handler that ends without one falls back, and past the last route the request goes on to the network, so an unanswered route never stalls a request. What a route sends on still passes the domain policy. Cancelling the call removes the route; a handler that fails ends it with `page_handler_failed`.
operations.name: page.route

operations.description: Answers a route's request by failing it with a network error its page sees, `failed` unless named; nothing reaches the network.
operations.name: route.abort

operations.description: Answers a route's request by sending it on, with any overrides, past every other route: the domain policy judges what it sends.
operations.name: route.continue

operations.description: Answers a route's request by passing it, with any overrides, to the route registered before, from the page's first route to the Session's last; past the last route it goes on to the network.
operations.name: route.fallback

operations.description: Sends a route's request on, with any overrides, past every other route, as `route.continue` does, and answers the response it got, its body kept; the handler then answers the request with `route.fulfill`, or, ending without one, the page gets that response.
operations.name: route.fetch

operations.description: Answers a route's request with a response of the program's own, or the one `route.fetch` returned with its changes; nothing reaches the network.
operations.name: route.fulfill

operations.description: Stops a Run at its next safe point, `stopped` and `incomplete`: no attempt in flight commits, and its work items return to pending. Answers its Run report; an ended Run's report is answered as it is. A Run whose engine died is stopped by this engine, which takes its writer role at the next run epoch; a Run another engine writes is stopped by that engine, the owner the Run index names.
operations.name: run.abort

operations.description: Writes a Checkpoint of a live Run now, through SQLite's online backup, where `location` says or where the engine keeps the Run's Checkpoints, and answers it once its file is complete, with its size, digest, run epoch and journal position. A Checkpoint the engine cannot write fails with `file_write_failed` and leaves no file.
operations.name: run.checkpoint

operations.description: Lets a Run finish and answers its Run report: a Run its program drives ends at once, `finished` and `complete`; a crawl ends once its work items are done, and a keep-alive crawl (`crawl.keep_alive`), which waits for new work while nothing is left, ends once this call lets it and its work items are done. A Run something stopped first answers its report saying `stopped`. A Run that ended `failed` fails the call with the error that failed it, and a write at its end that failed, such as its Plan file's, with that write's error. Cancelling the call, or its `timeout` passing, which fails it with `deadline_exceeded`, ends only the wait.
operations.name: run.finish

operations.description: Migrates a live Run: checkpoints it where `location` says or where the engine keeps its Checkpoints, then stops it at its next safe point, `stopped` with the stop reason `migrate`, to be resumed from that Checkpoint on another machine. Answers its Run report, which names the Checkpoint.
operations.name: run.migrate

operations.description: Opens a page in the Run's default Session, which the first call opens with the Run's settings and every later call shares; `page.session()` reaches it. The first page launches the Run's browser, so a missing browser build raises its code from this call.
operations.name: run.new_page

operations.description: Pauses a live Run: checkpoints it, then stops it at its next safe point, `stopped` with the stop reason `pause` and resumable by its Run ID with `run.resume`, after a restart too. Answers its Run report, which names the Checkpoint.
operations.name: run.pause

operations.description: Resumes an interrupted Run from its committed state, its run file on this machine or the Checkpoint `checkpoint` names: it takes the Run's writer lock and the next run epoch, so every write of an earlier writer is refused, and redoes the work since that state; its recorded Clean-up rules digest is kept. A live Run is answered as it is, `existing`; a finished one as it is. A Run bound to another machine fails with `session_bound_to_machine`, and a Checkpoint of a format version this engine cannot read with `format_version_unsupported`.
operations.name: run.resume

operations.description: Sets the program's own status line about a live Run, at most 512 characters, which replaces the one before: kept in the Run's state, so a resume keeps it, shown in its Run index row and carried on its progress, `run.progress`. Answers the Run's progress. A Run this engine does not run fails with `run_not_found`.
operations.name: run.set_progress_message

operations.description: Starts a Run its program drives, and answers once it is started. A Run ID names the Run for good: a start with an existing Run ID returns that Run as it is when the caller and the inputs match, and fails with `run_conflict` otherwise.
operations.name: run.start

operations.description: Stops a Run at its next safe point with a Checkpoint, `stopped` and `incomplete` as an abort by its program, resumable by its Run ID, and answers its Run report; an ended Run's report is answered as it is. The wait is bounded by `timeout.close`, or the call's `timeout`: past it, the call fails with `deadline_exceeded` and the Run still stops at its next safe point. A Run that ended `failed` fails the call as `run.finish` does.
operations.name: run.stop

operations.description: Answers what a Run used, as the Usage ledger charged it: its model calls and tokens, browser time, proxy bytes, requests, paid solves and Paid fetches, each Limit that applies to it with what is left of it, and whether it is uncapped. An ended Run answers its report's Usage.
operations.name: run.usage

operations.description: Repeats a text back to the caller.
operations.name: sample.echo

operations.description: Routes the requests of every page of the Session whose URL matches to the program, as `page.route` does, after the page's own routes.
operations.name: session.route

operations.description: Lists every Limit of the Usage ledger, by scope, with the Usage charged and held against it in its current period and what is left.
operations.name: usage.list

operations.description: Sets a Limit to a person's amount, in place of every Limit of its scope, Usage kind, currency and period but a managed Operator policy's, keeping the Usage counted. A person's answer: offered only in the Console and the interactive CLI prompt.
operations.name: usage.raise

operations.description: Adds a Limit of the caller's own to the Usage ledger, which holds beside the others: the tightest one holds, so it can only lower what applies. Answers it with its Usage.
operations.name: usage.set

settings.description: How many requests a Run admits in a minute at most, spaced evenly (GCRA), whatever its concurrency; none by default. An Operator policy cap bounds it even when unset, and a run already going takes a tightened cap at its next admission.
settings.name: admission.max_requests_per_minute

settings.description: Whether the Session's Chromium runs with no window: `true` by default. Headless or not, the site sees one browser's identity, with no `HeadlessChrome` token in its user agent.
settings.name: browser.headless

settings.description: How long a Pinned artifact no installed executable pins stays in the Browser cache unused before the clean-up deletes it, and how long an executable's entry counts as installed after it was last seen: 30 days. `null` turns the automatic clean-up off. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: browser_cache.max_unused_age

settings.description: How often a live Run writes a Checkpoint where the engine keeps its Checkpoints, on the engine's clock; none by default locally.
settings.name: checkpoint.interval

settings.description: The domains whose consent prompts a run accepts instead of refusing. A Recipe or a run only narrows it; it is widened only in configuration or by a person's answer.
settings.name: consent.domains

settings.description: Where the Daemon serves the Console, as `host:port`: `127.0.0.1` on port 7800 plus the major (7700 plus the minor during `0.y` previews), so each major's Console has its own port. Port 0 takes a free port, which the Daemon's runtime file and `daemon status` report. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: console.address

settings.description: Where `daemon run`, the foreground Daemon, listens, as `host:port`: `127.0.0.1` on port 7900 plus the major (7600 plus the minor during `0.y` previews). Port 0 takes a free port, which its log names. Only a loopback address, until the Daemon terminates TLS. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy, or for `daemon run` through `GOODFETCH_DAEMON_ADDRESS`.
settings.name: daemon.address

settings.description: How long `daemon run`, the foreground Daemon, drains on `SIGTERM` before it exits: 110 seconds, below the 120-second `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` of the Helm chart, which must exceed it. Each run that reaches its next safe point in that time stops with a Checkpoint, resumable by its Run ID; one that does not stays resumable from its run file. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy, or for `daemon run` through `GOODFETCH_DAEMON_DRAIN_GRACE` in milliseconds.
settings.name: daemon.drain_grace

settings.description: How long a Daemon with no connected Client, a visible Console tab included, waits before it stops: 10 minutes. `daemon start --keep-alive`, a held Schedule and an installed service keep it running. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: daemon.idle_timeout

settings.description: The hosts a run's requests may reach: each entry its host and their subdomains, matched on the host as a browser's URL parser leaves it (punycode, dotted-decimal IPv4), and `*` every host, only when written. `["*"]` by default; set for a connection or a Run. A request to a host it does not list fails with `egress_refused`.
settings.name: egress.allowed_domains

settings.description: The hosts no request of a run may reach, whatever `egress.allowed_domains` allows: each entry its host and their subdomains, matched as `egress.allowed_domains` matches, and `*` every host. Empty by default; set for a connection or a Run. A request to a host it lists fails with `egress_refused`.
settings.name: egress.blocked_domains

settings.description: Whether the engine opens no connection nobody configured: every pinned download, such as a Pinned artifact missing from the Browser cache, fails with `artifact_unavailable_offline` before it connects, naming the command that supplies it beforehand. `false` by default; set at every layer, and an Operator policy can lock it.
settings.name: egress.offline

settings.description: Extra Filter lists, by URL or path. Their scriptlets run only when the value comes from an Operator policy or user or project configuration; from a Recipe or a run, only their blocking rules apply.
settings.name: filter_lists.extra

settings.description: How an engine process writes its logs on stderr, or on stdout under `daemon run`: `text`, lines for a person reading a terminal, or `json`, JSON lines. Unset, the logs are text on stderr and JSON lines on stdout under `daemon run`; a log file holds JSON lines whatever it says. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: log.format

settings.description: Host names mapped to addresses before any lookup, in the engine's resolver and in Chromium, each address still checked by ADR 0017's resolved-address rule. Empty by default; an Operator policy can lock it.
settings.name: network.resolve

settings.description: Where `daemon run`, the foreground Daemon, serves its ops listener, as `host:port`: `/livez` and `/readyz` answer a status and no body to anyone, and `/metrics`, Prometheus' text, only with the ops token, the `ops.token` file of the major's folder, as a bearer token. Unset by default: no ops listener and no Prometheus export. Any address, so a cluster's probes and scrapers reach it; a request whose `Host` is a name other than `localhost`, or that carries an `Origin`, is refused. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy, or for `daemon run` through `GOODFETCH_OPS_ADDRESS`.
settings.name: ops.address

settings.description: The OTLP/HTTP endpoint `daemon run`, the foreground Daemon, exports its metrics to, in protobuf, every 60 seconds and once more as it exits: a full URL such as `http://collector:4318/v1/metrics`. Unset by default: nothing is exported (ADR 0043).
settings.name: otlp.metrics_endpoint

settings.description: The OTLP/HTTP endpoint an engine process exports its `tracing` spans to, such as `http://localhost:4318/v1/traces`; unset, the default, exports nothing, and nothing leaves the machine. The spans cover each run, page and CDP command, with glossary IDs and bounded values as fields and a URL as its origin. Span names, span fields and the engine's targets are Experimental: a minor may change them, and its release notes list the change. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: otlp.traces_endpoint

settings.description: How a Run shares Politeness with the other runs of its user: `shared` with every engine of the user (through the Politeness store when one is configured, else on the machine), `per_daemon` on the machine only, ignoring a store, or `run` for Politeness of its own. Anything but `shared` is listed in the Run's result.
settings.name: politeness.sharing

settings.description: How long the engine's HTTP transports let a connection attempt to one of a host's addresses run before they start the next one beside it: 250 ms, RFC 8305's Connection Attempt Delay. An attempt that fails starts the next at once.
settings.name: resolver.attempt_delay

settings.description: How long the engine's HTTP transports wait for a host's IPv6 addresses once its IPv4 addresses arrived first, before they start connecting over IPv4: 50 ms, RFC 8305's Resolution Delay.
settings.name: resolver.resolution_delay

settings.description: How a Run's commits reach the disk: `full`, the default, keeps every acknowledged commit through a power cut (`synchronous=FULL`, with `fullfsync` on macOS); `fast` (`synchronous=NORMAL`) survives a process crash only, since an OS crash or a power cut may roll back recent commits, possibly many, without damaging the run state. A Run in `fast` names it in its run report's `weakened`.
settings.name: run_state.durability

settings.description: The Secret reference of the key-encryption key that wraps each Run's data key, resolved when a Run starts: a Run whose reference does not resolve is refused with `secret_unavailable`. Taken only from an Operator policy and user and project configuration; none by default.
settings.name: run_state.key_reference

settings.description: Where Runs keep their run state: `per_run`, the default, one SQLite file in each run folder; `per_install`, one database, `run-state.sqlite` in the per-major folder, holding every Run of the install and major and written by the Daemon alone, to which an Attached engine then hands its Runs. Export, import and Checkpoint give the same per-run file in both. Taken only from the machine's own layers, and read when the Daemon starts.
settings.name: run_state.layout

settings.description: The folder that holds the run folders, each named by its Run ID; by default the per-user, per-major data folder of the Goodfetch home.
settings.name: run_state.location

settings.description: How many times the sample operation repeats a text.
settings.name: sample.echo_repeats

settings.description: Secrets are given by Secret reference, never as values, an honesty guarantee that stays locked whatever the layer.
settings.name: secrets.by_reference

settings.description: Where a Session's login comes from. A Recipe never sets or locks it; it may only expose it to its users.
settings.name: session.source

settings.description: How long a locator action waits for its target to be unique and actionable, and replays a gesture that landed elsewhere, before it fails with `deadline_exceeded`, or `target_not_unique` for a target still ambiguous: 30 s.
settings.name: timeout.action

settings.description: How long a stop of a Run, `run.stop` or a scope's close, waits for its next safe point before it fails with `deadline_exceeded`, the Run still stopping there: 30 s.
settings.name: timeout.close

settings.description: How long a request may wait for its response's first byte before its attempt fails with `deadline_exceeded`: 30 s.
settings.name: timeout.first_byte

settings.description: How long a navigation may take before its attempt fails with `deadline_exceeded`: 30 s, Playwright's default.
settings.name: timeout.navigation

settings.description: How long a Run may go on before it checkpoints and stops at its next safe point, resumable; none by default.
settings.name: timeout.run

settings.description: How long a Secret provider may take to answer one reference before the resolution fails with `secret_unavailable`, `failure: "timed_out"`: 30 s.
settings.name: timeout.secret

settings.description: Domains whose certificate may fail verification, each with a pin, `any`, or `null` for trust on first use. A pin and `any` are taken only from an Operator policy and user and project configuration; a Recipe or a run may list a domain only for trust on first use.
settings.name: tls.accept_invalid_certs

settings.description: Extra certificate authorities by domain: certificate files or Secret references. Taken only from an Operator policy and user and project configuration, never from a Recipe or a run.
settings.name: tls.trusted_cas

settings.description: Whether an executable more than three months past its release date prints one line a day on stderr saying so, from its own release date alone, with no network call. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: version.age_notice

settings.description: The domains whose Walls no run reads past, whatever another layer allows. Set only in an Operator policy.
settings.name: wall.denied_domains

settings.description: The domains whose Walls a run may read past by generic means. A Recipe or a run only narrows it; it is widened only in configuration or by a person's answer.
settings.name: wall.domains

settings.description: The domains on which reading past a Wall may fetch a page again. A Recipe or a run only narrows it; it is widened only in configuration, never by an answer.
settings.name: wall.refetch_domains

settings.description: Every webhook Goodfetch sends is signed, an honesty guarantee that stays locked whatever the layer.
